memos.scout:
The honest case for buying DOTF is thin, and the brief itself undercuts most of it.

What points toward demand: it's alive at 30.8 minutes, the last 15 minutes show net buy flow of 32.1 SOL across 17 buyers with only 0.1 SOL sold, and the price is up 1.6% over that window and 2.7% over 30 minutes. No airdrop dump was seen.

What argues hard against it: the launch was operator-controlled. Before graduation, the top 3 holders own 75% of the curve, one bundle accounts for 100% of curve buying, and the completer holds 72%. In the first two minutes after graduation, 4,001 SOL came from 8 buyers, with the top 5 accounting for essentially all of it, and a launch bot was present. That 4,001 SOL dwarfs the 32 SOL of recent organic-looking flow, so the recent buying is a trickle against a huge operator position that can exit at will. The 1.6% gain on $3,900 of volume rests on 2 sellers, a thin sample. Market cap of $115M on a $20 desk ticket and a 4,100 SOL pool is a fragile setup where round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% eat much of any small move.

Conclusion: there is no strong case for buying. The only positive signal is that recent flow has been mildly net-positive, which is not enough to offs
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss path is an operator exit. The first two minutes after graduation show 4,001 SOL bought by 8 buyers outside our agent, with top-5 buyer share at 99.99%, a launch bot present, and a bundle_share of 1.0. That is an operator position, not organic demand. Our 40-minute run is only 2.7%, and the last 15 minutes show 32.2 SOL bought against 0.1 SOL sold by 2 sellers, which looks like the operator's own wallets rather than broad buying. With the top 3 holders at 75% of the curve and completer_share at 71.8%, a single distribution would crush the pool, which holds about 4,100 SOL. Our $20 ticket plus the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost needs a sustained move to clear, and a dump would not give us an exit. Skip.
